tasks.short: Coordinate administrative support services, staff priorities and service performance.

steps.what: Collect service requests, incidents and updates from departments.
Categorise requests, check missing details and identify likely service owners.

loop.input: Free-text service request and approved service catalogue.
loop.output: Suggested service category, missing fields and service queue.
loop.check: Allow listed categories only; validate required fields and route ambiguous or sensitive requests for review.
loop.stop: One classification pass per request; unmatched requests enter the coordinator's exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Forms and rules cover structured requests; varied mailbox descriptions need limited text interpretation.

steps.what: Set priorities and balance capacity against urgent service needs.
Brief service leads, resolve conflicts and agree responsibilities.
Record agreed actions, responsible leads and due dates.
Copy service progress into a separate weekly status sheet.
Review service trends and agree corrective changes with department leads.

tasks.design: Configure {HELPDESK} intake and connect agreed actions to {PROJECT}, using a bounded loop only to suggest categories for free-text requests. A {BI} dashboard replaces the copied status sheet, while managers set priorities, agree staff assignments and resolve service conflicts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrived through several channels, service categories were inconsistent and reporting depended on copied updates.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured intake, simple integrations and source-linked dashboards can remove coordination work; limited text classification handles informal requests.
tasks.still_hard: Cross-department priorities, unreliable progress updates and limited capacity still require active management.
tasks.human_edge: The manager recognises competing needs, negotiates service expectations and supports staff through difficult interactions.

ambition.what: A coordinated administrative support package for opening a satellite office.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from collecting status to resolving bottlenecks and improving service design. The manager can seek authority to rebalance a small shared service budget across agreed service targets.

reach.task: Plan the administrative workstream for a satellite-office opening.
reach.learn: Dependencies, milestones, capacity planning and acceptance criteria.

reach.task: Coordinate workplace incidents with administrative service queues.
reach.learn: Incident severity, contractor boundaries and workplace service targets.

evidence.claim: Configured queues, action records and source-linked dashboards can replace repeated status copying.
Bounded classification can suggest service categories; organisational priority and staff allocation remain human decisions.

assumptions: The department coordinates records, mail, office support and related workplace requests.
Some requests already enter {HELPDESK}; {EMAIL} and {CHAT} still connect departments.
The coordination-heavy prior is retained, but the copied reporting step offers a clear elimination opportunity.
Classification chooses service categories, not employee performance scores or automated staff assignments.
Build ranges cover a first set of service queues and include applicable consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Which services and staff fall within the manager's remit?
Which request channels and action registers are authoritative?
Are service targets and escalation responsibilities agreed?
Would proposed reporting introduce employee monitoring requiring consultation under national rules?
Is a satellite-office opening a realistic service opportunity?
research_questions: What share of requests can structured intake handle without a model?
Can existing {HELPDESK} reporting replace a separate {BI} dashboard?
Which missing updates reflect unclear ownership rather than a technical gap?
new_work: Review ambiguous request categories and sensitive exceptions.
Maintain the service catalogue and escalation routes.
Resolve duplicate requests and failed synchronisation.
Check dashboard freshness and source-data quality.
Review whether measures encourage useful service outcomes.
tasks.statement: Direct or coordinate the supportive services department of a business, agency, or organization.

tasks.short: Set departmental goals and deadlines against service needs, capacity, and organisational priorities.

steps.what: Review organisational priorities, service results, commitments, and available capacity.
Compare possible goals and deadlines against workload and capacity.
Discuss priorities, dependencies, and feasible commitments with team leads.
Choose departmental goals, deadlines, measures, and accountable leads.
Record approved goals, assign deadlines, and notify accountable leads.

tasks.design: Configure a planning view in {BI} and a goal register in {PROJECT}, using agreed priorities and capacity data. A deterministic scenario calculator tests manager-entered goals and deadlines; people negotiate commitments and approve the selected plan before assignments and reminders are created.
tasks.previous_blocker: Priorities and capacity assumptions lived in separate documents, while the central work involved negotiating competing demands.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured planning views and a small scenario calculator can make preparation cheaper without trying to automate goal selection.
tasks.still_hard: Capacity estimates are uncertain, dependencies cross departments, and goals can reward the wrong behaviour. Agreement and accountability remain human work.
tasks.human_edge: Choose which service outcomes matter and secure commitments that people believe are achievable.
tasks.altitude: Preparation and recording take less time, leaving more room to negotiate realistic commitments. The manager can revisit priorities more often within existing authority; budget and staffing rights do not change.

reach.task: Maintain a capacity-constrained departmental delivery plan.
reach.learn: Effort estimation, dependencies, and explicit contingency.

evidence.claim: Deterministic capacity scenarios can support planning without selecting organisational priorities.
Goal negotiation and commitment remain substantial human work.

assumptions: Goals concern departmental services rather than automated individual performance assessment.
The manager already has authority to set departmental priorities within an agreed budget.
Build ranges cover a departmental planning aid with aggregate capacity data.
GDPR applies where planning inputs contain personal data; consultation requirements depend on national rules.
unknowns: Who must approve goals that affect other departments?
How reliable are workload and capacity estimates?
Can the existing {PROJECT} provide the required register and reminders?
Would the proposed planning view introduce employee monitoring?
research_questions: Which constraints most often make departmental deadlines unrealistic?
Which scenario calculations would change an actual planning decision?
Can aggregate capacity replace named employee data?
new_work: Maintain capacity assumptions and dependency records.
Check that scenario outputs reflect actual working constraints.
Review whether chosen measures encourage useful service outcomes.
tasks.statement: Set goals and deadlines for the department.

tasks.short: Prepare operational reports, check their accuracy, and review service schedules.

steps.what: Download service activity, spending, and schedule records.
Combine extracts and check totals, dates, and missing entries.
Resolve missing entries and conflicting figures with service owners.
Prepare the operational report with figures, explanations, and outstanding issues.

loop.input: Validated figures, service owner notes, unresolved exceptions, and report template.
loop.output: Report commentary linked to source records; tables come from deterministic calculations.
loop.check: Check every numerical reference against calculated tables; the manager reviews explanations and unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per report; missing evidence produces an explicit gap and manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables need no model, but variable service notes need concise, contextual explanation.

steps.what: Approve the report and decide schedule changes for service shortfalls.
Circulate the approved report and schedule to service owners.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration brings approved extracts from the {OPS_SYSTEM}, {ERP}, and {PROJECT} into the {DATA_PLATFORM}, with validation rules and a {BI} view. An artefact generator produces tables and uses a bounded loop for source-linked commentary in {DOCS}; the manager approves reports and schedule changes before configured notifications run.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different reporting definitions, manual exports, and service explanations made repeatable reporting costly to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing export scheduling and inexpensive deterministic code can handle collection and checks. A bounded model loop can draft commentary from uneven notes.
tasks.still_hard: Missing records and disputed measures still need service owners. Schedule decisions require knowledge of capacity and service commitments.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether a reported improvement reflects better service, delayed work, or a misleading measure.

ambition.what: Weekly intervention decisions on administrative service backlogs.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling reports to investigating exceptions and choosing service interventions. Faster evidence supports existing scheduling authority; it grants no additional spending rights.

reach.task: Define measures that distinguish service demand, capacity, and avoidable delay.
reach.learn: Metric definitions, basic variation analysis, and source reconciliation.

reach.task: Identify dependencies behind schedule slippage.
reach.learn: Dependency mapping and capacity planning.

evidence.claim: Scheduled imports, validation rules, and templated reports can automate much of report preparation.
Service explanations and schedule trade-offs still require contextual review.

assumptions: The typical department has structured service records and supplements them with documents and spreadsheets.
Build ranges cover one department and a limited set of recurring reports, using available exports.
Personal data is minimised and access-controlled under GDPR; employee consultation follows applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which systems contain authoritative service and schedule records?
Are report definitions agreed across service owners?
Which exports, interfaces, and access permissions are available?
Do reports contain identifiable employee activity data requiring consultation?
research_questions: Which report sections directly change a service decision?
Which validation rules catch the most consequential reporting errors?
Can existing reporting configuration remove the need for a custom integration?
new_work: Review generated commentary and unresolved data exceptions.
Maintain metric definitions, source mappings, and distribution permissions.
Investigate failed imports and reconcile changed source formats.
tasks.statement: Prepare and review operational reports and schedules to ensure accuracy and efficiency.

tasks.short: Investigate administrative processes and implement approved procedural or policy improvements.

steps.what: Collect process records, policies, costs, and service complaints.
Interview staff and observe how the process works in practice.
Compare delays, costs, controls, and improvement scenarios.
Draft a recommended procedure or policy change and implementation plan.

loop.input: Current policy text, source-linked process analysis, manager-selected scenario, and staff concerns.
loop.output: A change proposal identifying revised clauses, expected effects, assumptions, and rollout steps.
loop.check: Require source references and a clause comparison; the manager checks feasibility and routes legal questions.
loop.stop: One proposal and one revision pass; unresolved policy conflicts remain flagged for a person.
loop.why_not_simpler: Calculations are deterministic, but combining varied policies and staff concerns into coherent wording needs text interpretation.

steps.what: Consult affected teams and relevant advisers or employee representatives.
Approve the policy change, scope, controls, and rollout conditions.
Configure approved process changes and release updated procedures.
Compare post-change results with the baseline and report unresolved issues.

tasks.design: Bring permitted process records into the {DATA_PLATFORM} and calculate baseline measures and scenarios for {BI}. A bounded drafting loop prepares source-linked proposals in {DOCS}; consultation and policy approval stay human, while {WORKFLOW} supports approved rollout and outcome tracking.
tasks.previous_blocker: Process evidence was fragmented, analysis was bespoke, and policy changes required knowledge held by staff and advisers.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable data checks and scenario code reduce analytical preparation. Bounded text drafting can make policy comparisons cheaper while retaining human approval.
tasks.still_hard: Measured improvements may reflect changes in demand rather than the intervention. Records disposal requires validated retention rules, legal-hold checks, and separately authorised destruction; consultation requirements vary under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a flawed process from a necessary control, and negotiate changes that staff can actually use.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time observing work, testing explanations, and securing adoption. Reusable evidence can support other departments, but policy approval and records-destruction rights remain with their existing owners.

reach.task: Evaluate whether a process pilot caused the observed improvement.
reach.learn: Baseline design, comparison groups where feasible, and alternative explanations.

reach.task: Translate approved retention schedules into practical record-handling procedures.
reach.learn: Record classification, retention triggers, legal holds, and disposal evidence.

evidence.claim: Records applications, deterministic measures, and bounded report drafting can support process improvement.
Policy approval, consultation, and causal interpretation remain human responsibilities.
GDPR Article 22 constrains solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects on people.

assumptions: Build ranges cover one process pilot and its supporting evidence and approval workflow.
The pilot supports departmental process analysis rather than individual employee scoring.
GDPR applies to personal data; any employment-related AI use needs separate assessment under the EU AI Act.
The access and consultation range includes adviser review and employee consultation where required by national rules; formal procedures may take longer.
The initial rollout does not execute irreversible records destruction.
unknowns: Which process and measurable service problem should the pilot address?
Who has policy approval and records-disposal authority?
Which retention rules, legal holds, and consultation obligations apply?
Do available records support a credible baseline without employee-level monitoring?
Which rollout changes need technical support beyond departmental configuration?
research_questions: Which apparent delays represent necessary controls?
What evidence would distinguish a useful intervention from normal demand variation?
Can the proposed change first be tested in a reversible, limited pilot?
new_work: Maintain process definitions, source mappings, and proposal templates.
Review drafted policy wording and unresolved evidence gaps.
Document consultation outcomes and approval conditions.
Check rollout configuration and investigate unintended effects.
Maintain retention and legal-hold rules with the responsible advisers.
tasks.statement: Analyze internal processes and recommend and implement procedural or policy changes to improve operations, such as supply changes or the disposal of records.

tasks.short: Replenish office supplies, receive deliveries, store stock, and distribute items.

steps.what: Inspect supply cupboards and count available stock.
Calculate replenishment quantities from counts, requests, and expected usage.
Review quantities, budget, and exceptions before approving the requisition.
Create and send the approved purchase order.
Receive deliveries and inspect quantities, damage, and substitutions.
Record received quantities and flag delivery discrepancies.
Move supplies into labelled storage locations.
Pick and distribute requested supplies to employees.
Update the stock record for issued quantities.

tasks.design: Configure a stock register and simple receipt and issue forms in {WORKFLOW}, linked to catalogue items and purchasing approvals in {PROCUREMENT}. Reorder rules draft requisitions, approved requisitions generate orders, and confirmed receipts update stock; people still inspect, store, and distribute supplies.
tasks.previous_blocker: Small stock values seldom justified bespoke integrations, and unrecorded cupboard withdrawals made stock balances unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, catalogue purchasing, and approval configuration can remove repeated entry. AI-assisted coding can lower the cost of any small connector that remains necessary.
tasks.still_hard: Physical handling remains. Stock accuracy depends on recording withdrawals, while urgent requests and substitutions still require judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Notice damaged goods, unsuitable substitutions, and practical needs that a stock balance cannot explain.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time calculating orders and chasing receipt records. Physical work and existing purchasing decision rights remain; the main gain is more reliable replenishment.

reach.task: Maintain accurate receipts and location-level stock records.
reach.learn: Cycle counting, receipt exceptions, and simple stock controls.

reach.task: Review reorder levels against consumption and delivery lead times.
reach.learn: Demand variability, lead-time uncertainty, and stockout trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Catalogue purchasing, approval routing, and reorder rules can automate office-supply paperwork.
Software alone does not remove delivery inspection, storage, or physical distribution.

assumptions: The typical company uses {PROCUREMENT} for orders but may keep office stock in a spreadsheet.
Orders are sent only against approved requisitions; changed prices or quantities return for approval.
Receipt forms prefill order lines, but a person confirms actual delivery quantities.
Build ranges assume existing purchasing interfaces and ordinary office supplies.
GDPR applies to requester records; access is limited and consultation follows national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Does {PROCUREMENT} already support stock records and reorder thresholds?
Who records withdrawals from shared cupboards?
Which purchases require approval and which have delegated limits?
Are supplier catalogue and order interfaces available?
research_questions: Would a small set of standard stock items remove most urgent orders?
Is recording individual issues worth the effort compared with periodic counts?
Can existing purchasing configuration replace a separate stock register?
new_work: Maintain item codes, reorder levels, approved substitutes, and supplier lead times.
Reconcile physical counts with recorded balances.
Handle failed orders, price changes, and delivery discrepancies.
Maintain form access and purchasing approval limits.

tasks.short: Plan and control spending on administrative contracts, equipment and supplies.

steps.what: Collect actual spending, open orders and existing budget balances.
Read contract renewals, price changes and equipment replacement plans.

loop.input: Supplier contracts, renewal notices and equipment plans.
loop.output: Cost assumptions with amounts, dates, conditions and source passages.
loop.check: Validate currencies, dates and totals; require a source passage and manager acceptance for each assumption.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document; ambiguous terms remain unresolved for review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Renewal and indexation terms vary in free text; arithmetic after extraction is deterministic.

steps.what: Reconcile spending and commitments, then calculate forecast scenarios.
Agree service priorities and trade spending against operational needs.
Approve the proposed budget or return it for revision.
Enter approved allocations and communicate spending limits.
Review variances and decide corrective action.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration reconciles {ERP} actuals with {PROCUREMENT} commitments and feeds a scenario dashboard in {BI}. A bounded loop extracts contract assumptions from {CLM} for review; approved allocations enter {ERP} through configured approvals, and variance alerts return decisions to the manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: Commitments, invoices and contract terms used different identifiers and reporting dates; local reconciliation was cheaper than integration.
tasks.enabler_now: Small integrations and deterministic scenario calculations are easier to build; bounded extraction can handle varied contract wording.
tasks.still_hard: Accrual timing, incomplete commitments and service trade-offs still require finance knowledge and negotiation.
tasks.human_edge: The manager judges which reductions would damage service and negotiates acceptable priorities.

ambition.what: Weekly decisions on discretionary equipment replacement using current commitments.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling forecasts and more time testing service choices. A delegated equipment-replacement limit could add decision rights, subject to budget-holder agreement.

reach.task: Compare administrative service costs under different demand scenarios.
reach.learn: Cost drivers, accruals and how to distinguish correlation from avoidable cost.

evidence.claim: Commitment reconciliation, budget arithmetic and threshold alerts are deterministic once accounting rules are agreed.
Contract extraction can propose sourced assumptions, but conditional clauses require review.

assumptions: Finance retains control of accounting treatment and formal budget approval.
A {SPREADSHEET} commonly joins exports and assumptions even where {ERP} budget features exist.
The judgement-heavy prior is retained; structured inputs make preparation easier to automate than spending decisions.
Build ranges cover one administrative budget perimeter and a limited set of contract formats.
unknowns: Can {ERP} expose actuals, accruals and open commitments without double counting?
Are supplier and cost-centre identifiers consistent across systems?
Which budget features are already licensed and configured?
What spending authority can the manager receive?
research_questions: Can reconciliation reproduce the finance team's accepted period totals?
Which contract terms account for most manual extraction exceptions?
Would existing {ERP} forecasting features remove the need for custom scenario code?
new_work: Resolve unmatched commitments and accounting-period differences.
Review extracted renewal and price assumptions.
Maintain cost mappings and forecast drivers.
Check alert thresholds and integration failures.
tasks.statement: Plan, administer, and control budgets for contracts, equipment, and supplies.

tasks.short: Hire administrative staff and manage terminations with human employment decisions.

steps.what: Confirm the staffing need or proposed termination and required authority.
Assemble role documents or authorised employee records for the case.
For hiring, arrange interviews and collect candidate documents.
Interview candidates and assess evidence against agreed role requirements.
Choose a candidate and approve proposed employment terms.
For termination, examine grounds, procedure, alternatives and national requirements.
Decide whether termination is justified and authorised.
Explain the termination decision and discuss the employee's questions and next steps.
Prepare, check and issue the applicable offer or termination documents.
Update employment records and trigger the approved joining or leaving checklist.

tasks.design: Configured workflows in {ATS}, {HCM} and {CALENDAR} assemble authorised records, arrange interviews and track required actions. Approved templates in {DOCS} populate documents for HR review before release through {ESIGN}; confirmed employment events trigger {WORKFLOW} checklists and requests to {PAYROLL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sensitive records crossed departmental boundaries, templates varied, and employment decisions could not be reduced to routing rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing workflow features and limited integrations can remove repeated collection and entry without automating employment judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Fair assessment, disputed evidence, employee representation and termination requirements under national rules remain case-specific.
tasks.human_edge: People assess suitability, hear the employee's account, weigh alternatives and take responsibility for decisions.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time chasing documents and arranging interviews, with more time for candidate assessment and employee conversations. Employment decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.role: executive secretary and executive administrative assistant
reach.task: Coordinate confidential interview and employment-case logistics.
reach.learn: Restricted record access, neutral candidate communication and escalation boundaries.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, template population and approved lifecycle updates can use configuration without model-based candidate scoring.
GDPR Article 22 restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, subject to its conditions and exceptions.
Recruitment and certain worker-management AI uses fall within the EU AI Act's listed high-risk categories; intended use matters.
The EU AI Act includes prior information duties to workers and representatives for workplace deployment of high-risk AI.

assumptions: Hiring and termination are alternative branches; shares describe a mixed workload, not one employee's sequence.
The administrative services manager acts as hiring manager for their team.
No model ranks candidates, assesses employees or recommends termination.
Termination follows applicable national procedures, including employee hearings and representation where required.
Build ranges include restricted access review and applicable employee or works-council consultation; formal procedures may take longer.
unknowns: Which national employment and consultation rules apply?
Who holds hiring, offer and termination authority?
Which records may each role access and how long may they be retained?
Which templates and employment-event interfaces are already approved?
What is the actual mix of hiring and termination work?
research_questions: Can configured workflows cover both branches without copying sensitive records into a separate store?
Do access tests prevent hiring coordinators from seeing termination files?
Which document variants still require individual legal review?
new_work: Maintain national document variants and approval routes.
Review documents before external release.
Resolve missing approvals, disputed dates and failed record updates.
Review access permissions, retention and audit logs.
Complete consultation required for the actual deployment.
tasks.statement: Hire and terminate clerical and administrative personnel.

tasks.short: Teach staff administrative procedures and check their understanding.

steps.what: Find current procedures and identify what staff need to learn.
Prepare examples, instructions and practice exercises.

loop.input: Approved procedure, session brief and training template.
loop.output: Training pack with examples, exercises and procedure references.
loop.check: Check references and required sections automatically; the manager checks accuracy and teaching value.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported instructions go back to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle layout; varied procedure text needs interpretation to create useful examples.

steps.what: Arrange attendance, timing and room or call access.
Demonstrate procedures, explain exceptions and answer staff questions.
Observe practice and decide who needs further help.
Record attendance and learning checks, then arrange follow-up.

tasks.design: An integration retrieves approved procedures from {DOCS} and completion records from {LMS}; a bounded drafting loop prepares a training pack for review. Configured flows in {LMS} and {CALENDAR} handle bookings and records, while the manager teaches and checks practical understanding.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedure versions, training records and bookings were separate; preparing good examples still required reading.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling features and small integrations cover administration; bounded drafting can shorten preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Teaching unfamiliar staff, spotting confusion and handling sensitive questions remain demanding.
tasks.human_edge: The manager notices hesitation, adapts explanations and establishes confidence to ask questions.

ambition.what: Short procedure clinics for evening and remote administrative staff.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less preparation and booking work, leaving room for targeted coaching. Training sign-off rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Maintain a procedure question log after each session.
reach.learn: Plain-language instructions, document versioning and when to escalate an exception.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, attendance recording and template assembly can use configuration and deterministic integrations.
Procedure-based drafting is feasible with source checks and human review; teaching quality still needs local validation.

assumptions: The baseline is a recurring instructor-led procedure class, not a regulated qualification.
The conversation-heavy prior is retained; preparation and administration offer the main savings.
Build ranges cover a first procedure family using existing systems, not a company-wide content migration.
unknowns: Which procedures are approved and current?
Does the {LMS} support attendance imports and follow-up bookings?
Which staff need language, accessibility or shift-specific support?
Do national rules require employee consultation for changes to training records?
research_questions: Can staff complete the procedure correctly after using the generated exercises?
How much preparation time survives the manager's accuracy review?
new_work: Review drafted examples against current procedures.
Correct missing or outdated procedure references.
Maintain booking rules and integration access.
Resolve attendance and completion-record exceptions.
tasks.statement: Conduct classes to teach procedures to staff.

tasks.short: Guide vendors, resolve service problems and agree actions that meet administrative service needs.

steps.what: Collect service requirements, contract terms and recent service issues.
Clarify priorities and acceptable service trade-offs with internal service owners.
Prepare vendor guidance and questions using agreed priorities.

loop.input: Approved service priorities and a permission-filtered service evidence pack.
loop.output: Vendor briefing with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate references and quoted amounts; manager checks proposed wording before using it.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; missing evidence leaves marked gaps for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Service issues and requests contain free text that templates cannot reliably connect.

steps.what: Discuss service problems, explain requirements and agree feasible actions with the vendor.
Record agreed actions, owners and deadlines in the service action log.

loop.input: Manager's meeting notes and agreed service actions.
loop.output: Proposed action records with owners, dates and supporting note passages.
loop.check: Validate owner identities and dates; manager confirms commitments before records become active.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; ambiguous commitments remain unassigned drafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Meeting notes express commitments in varied language and often omit an explicit owner or date.

steps.what: Send deadline reminders and escalate overdue service actions.

tasks.design: An integration gathers permission-filtered service evidence from {PROCUREMENT}, {DOCS} and {HELPDESK}; a bounded drafting loop prepares a vendor briefing. The manager conducts the discussion and confirms extracted commitments before they enter {PROJECT}, where configured reminders track agreed deadlines.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence sits across service records and correspondence. Interpreting disputed commitments needs context, while custom connectors were costly to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce connector and validation work. Bounded text extraction can prepare briefings and action records without taking over vendor relationships.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed scope, weak service evidence and vendors lacking structured access remain difficult. Contract changes need the organization's existing authorization route.
tasks.human_edge: Recognizing a strained relationship, testing promises and negotiating a workable recovery plan.

ambition.what: A monthly service recovery clinic for vendors with recurring unresolved issues.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less evidence chasing and more service recovery discussions. Existing negotiation and spending authority stays unchanged.

reach.task: Prioritize recurring building-service failures for vendor review.
reach.learn: Learn service criticality, response obligations and how failure records support escalation.

evidence.claim: Structured action records and deadline rules can automate reminders; disputed vendor conversations remain human.
The digest reports automated supplier negotiations, but that case does not establish suitability for service recovery conversations.

assumptions: The baseline is recurring office-service coordination in a mid-size European company.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors.
Routine reminders repeat confirmed commitments and cannot change scope, price or contractual terms.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for one service team and a small set of connectors.
Access work includes GDPR checks and consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which service agreements and issue records are accessible in structured form.
Who may agree service changes and spending commitments.
Whether vendors accept reminders at designated contact addresses.
Operating countries, applicable national consultation arrangements and internal access lead times.
research_questions: Can the relevant {PROCUREMENT} and {HELPDESK} interfaces preserve record permissions and revision references?
How reliably can action extraction distinguish agreed commitments from suggestions in representative meeting notes?
new_work: Check draft briefings and extracted commitments.
Resolve missing owners, disputed dates and stale service records.
Maintain reminder recipients, escalation rules and connector permissions.
tasks.statement: Communicate with and provide guidance for external vendors and service providers to ensure the organization, department, or work unit's business needs are met.

tasks.short: Develop, test, approve and publish operational standards and procedures for administrative services.

steps.what: Gather existing procedures, service requirements and examples of recurring exceptions.
Agree the procedure's scope, service standards and exception responsibilities with affected staff.
Write the procedure, responsibilities, controls and practical instructions.

loop.input: Approved procedure requirements, current source documents and a fixed procedure template.
loop.output: Draft procedure with source references, version metadata and unresolved policy questions.
loop.check: Validate required sections and references; manager checks feasibility and unsupported obligations.
loop.stop: One draft and two targeted repairs; unresolved conflicts return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Sources contain varied prose and exceptions requiring synthesis into usable instructions.

steps.what: Walk through realistic cases and identify impractical instructions or missing exceptions.
Resolve test findings and submit the revised procedure for approval.
Approve the procedure and release the controlled version to affected staff.

tasks.design: A deterministic collector assembles current records from {DOCS} and {HELPDESK}, and a bounded drafting loop fills a controlled procedure template. Staff test realistic cases, the manager resolves findings, and configured approval and publication in {DOCS} release only the authorized version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates helped formatting but could not reconcile scattered narrative sources. Procedure development also depends on agreement about responsibilities and acceptable exceptions.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-linked drafting and inexpensive validation code can reduce compilation work. Existing versioning and approval features can handle controlled release.
tasks.still_hard: A polished draft can conceal an impractical process. Conflicting requirements and changes affecting employment conditions still need expert review and applicable national consultation.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing workable standards and securing agreement from the people who must use them.

ambition.what: Monthly decisions on procedure changes prompted by recurring service exceptions.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time testing procedures with staff and less time assembling documents. Publication authority remains with the existing approver.

reach.task: Assess whether a revised administrative procedure reduces delays and rework.
reach.learn: Learn process mapping, baseline measures and how to separate policy problems from execution problems.

evidence.claim: Controlled templates, versioning and approval workflows can automate procedure assembly and publication controls.
Source-linked drafting can reduce writing effort, while practical validation and policy choices remain human.

assumptions: Existing procedures and exceptions can be retrieved without broadening staff access.
The department head is the illustrative release approver; actual delegated authority may differ.
Time shares and remaining percentages are estimates; original policy judgement remains substantial.
Build ranges cover one procedure family, access, staff trials and initial rollout.
Consultation estimates include screening under national rules; formal proceedings may extend elapsed time.
GDPR applies to personal data in examples; the EU AI Act requires assessment if the eventual use extends into regulated employment decisions.
unknowns: Which procedures are current and who owns each source.
Whether existing {DOCS} approval and versioning features are enabled.
Which changes need specialist, employee-representative or department approval.
Operating countries and applicable collective agreements.
research_questions: Can {DOCS} enforce approval against the exact revision being published?
Which source-reference and contradiction checks catch material drafting errors in representative procedures?
new_work: Review source references and unresolved policy questions.
Maintain templates, ownership metadata and review dates.
Run staff walkthroughs and retire superseded versions.
tasks.statement: Develop operational standards and procedures for the work unit or department.

tasks.short: Organize administrative staff coverage, daily assignments and work procedures.

steps.what: Collect service demand, approved availability and outstanding administrative work.
Set coverage priorities, required skills and procedure constraints for the planning period.
Construct a draft schedule and allocate daily work across available staff.
Discuss coverage gaps, staff preferences and exceptional assignments with affected staff.
Authorize and circulate the staff schedule and daily work instructions.
Check new absences, urgent requests and overdue work during the day.
Reassign work and issue a revised schedule when coverage changes.

tasks.design: Read approved availability from {HCM} and work demand from {HELPDESK} and {PROJECT}; deterministic scheduling rules propose coverage and expose unmet constraints. tasks.short: Learn new office technologies through relevant guidance, demonstrations and practical use.

steps.what: Locate approved guidance and training for newly introduced office technology.
Read relevant guidance and choose administrative tasks to practise.
Attend a demonstration and ask questions about unfamiliar operations.
Practise representative tasks in the office application training environment and resolve errors.
Write a practical reference guide from tested operations and resolved questions.

loop.input: Approved guidance, tested practice results and resolved technology questions.
loop.output: Short reference guide with source references and application-version details.
loop.check: Validate references; learner checks instructions against successful practice and marks unresolved questions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; unsupported instructions are omitted for manual resolution.

tasks.previous_blocker: Guidance was hard to locate and often too broad for local tasks. Finding information faster could not replace learning through practice.

ambition.what: Short assisted practice sessions for part-time administrative staff who miss scheduled demonstrations.

reach.learn: Learn to distinguish missing training, access problems and interface defects using reproducible examples.
